mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticate as notarized by a licensed local notary, then apply the single applicable treaty path: if the country of origin is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, obtain only an Apostille from that country's competent authority; if not a party, obtain only consular legalization through the relevant ministry, the PRC Embassy or Consulate, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs sequence. The Hague Apostille path and the Consular Legalization path are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, supervisors, senior managers, authorized signatories, and any person with economic interest of 25% or more must be screened before incorporation against the domestic PRC sanctions and social-credit enforcement lists, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the OFAC Foreign Sanctions Evaders List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Interpol red notices. Exact-match screening, fuzzy Pinyin and native-script transliteration matching, date-of-birth and passport-number normalization, and negative-news checks are mandatory. A candidate with any confirmed match must be excluded; a similarity score above 80% triggers enhanced due diligence, documented risk rationalization, and compliance-committee approval. PEP status must be identified for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates, with source-of-wealth verification and heightened ongoing monitoring for a minimum of 12 months after the commercial relationship begins.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered statutory name of a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must be in simplified Chinese characters and must satisfy the four-tier structure of administrative division, specific trade name, industry or business characteristic, and legal form. English, Pinyin, and other foreign script have no statutory force and cannot appear alone in the registered name. A foreign investor's source-language name may be rendered through Mandarin phonetic transliteration, and a separate English trade name may be registered only as a self-used name once the Chinese statutory name is cleared. No homophonic or distorted characters that create public confusion with an existing registered trademark or enterprise are allowed.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon official rejection of the reserved name, the applicant or its filing attorney may, within 15 working days from service of the refusal notice, submit a written administrative reconsideration petition to the SAMR department that issued the refusal or to its superior administrative body under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China. The petition must attach the original refusal notice, at least three alternative name candidates in simplified Chinese, evidence of distinctive trade name use, and a compliance undertaking showing avoidance of all prohibited tokens. If reconsideration is dismissed or not accepted, the applicant may initiate administrative litigation before the competent People's Court within 15 days after service of the reconsideration decision, or may simultaneously file a fresh name pre-approval application using a substantially changed trade name during the residual reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or mail-forwarding address alone is not acceptable as a registered office in China and will be rejected by SAMR, the municipal tax bureau, and bank account opening KYC. For an overseas public-relations communications joint venture under ISIC 7310 and NAICS 541820, an actual fixed place of business is mandatory, evidenced by a lease in the legal name of the company, dedicated workstations, local staff presence, installed VAT invoice equipment, and the physical availability of accounting books, corporate chops, and service-of-process documents. A serviced-office or business-incubator lease may be tolerated only if the lease agreement expressly permits official inspection, the office is open during business hours, and the company name is visibly displayed on site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) original lease contract in the legal entity's name; (2) physical company name plate and office signage; (3) employment and social-insurance records located on site; (4) tax invoice system installed and operational at the registered address; (5) statutory books, board resolutions, and bank correspondence stored locally; (6) utility and property-management bills matching the registered address. The quantified risk of an unannounced SAMR or municipal tax inspection is moderate-high for a new Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture in the PR communications industry, estimated at 45% probability during the first 12 months, escalating beyond 70% if the registered address cannot demonstrate business substance, if turnover filings are inconsistent with bank receipts, or if the office is a virtual address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 1-54 and 68-83; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 7 and 10-12; Measures for the Registration of Market Entities (2021), Chapter III; Interim Measures for Foreign Investment Information Reporting (2020)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local Municipal/District Market Supervision and Administration Bureau; through the National Enterprise Registration One-Stop Online Portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Formation and Registration of a Limited Liability Company together with the Articles of Association and the Foreign Investment Information Report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture limited liability company in China. The shareholders freely fix the subscribed registered capital amount and the contribution schedule in the Articles of Association. No blocked escrow account requirement exists under national law, but the foreign shareholder's inbound capital contribution must be received and registered through a designated bank account in compliance with State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) reporting rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_JV_LTD

WHEREAS CN_JV_LTD (the 'Company') is a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture limited liability company being formed under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China; and

WHEREAS the shareholders have executed the Joint Venture Contract and Articles of Association establishing the subscribed registered capital, corporate purpose, governance architecture, and initial management framework; and

WHEREAS the directors named in the Articles of Association are present at this duly convened first board meeting and constitute a lawful quorum;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. Share Capital Subscription. The formation-stage capital subscriptions set out in the Articles of Association are ratified and accepted. The Board confirms the aggregate subscribed registered capital and acknowledges that shareholder contributions may be made in money or in kind as permitted by law. Management is authorized to open the required capital settlement account, receive contributions, verify remittances, and issue contribution certificates.

2. Banking Authorization. The Board appoints a licensed commercial bank operating in mainland China as principal depositary and settlement bank. The legal representative and the finance officer are authorized, jointly, to open accounts, sign deposit and operating documents, establish internet banking credentials, and carry out recurring treasury operations. The Board resolves that every foreign exchange inflow and outflow shall be reported to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange through the designated bank.

3. Registered Office. The registered office set out in the Articles of Association is adopted as the Company's statutory seat. The legal representative is authorized to execute lease documents, collect service of process, and file domicile changes with the State Administration for Market Regulation.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following statutory officers are appointed: [Name] as legal representative and general manager; [Name] as director and company secretary; and [Name] as supervisor. The supervisor shall not simultaneously be a director or manager and shall supervise the legality of management decisions.

5. Delegation and Implementation. The form of all official seals, bank mandates, and tax registration forms is approved. Officers are directed to complete all filings required by the Market Entity Registration Regulations and the State Taxation Administration. Any officer or agent may sign, execute, and deliver all grants of authority, certificates, and ancillary instruments necessary to carry out this resolution.

This resolution is valid from the date of establishment and remains in force until amended by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Business Scope Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration Online Portal operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Name Pre-approval Application to the competent Market Supervision Administration through the SAMR National Enterprise Registration online portal. On the electronic form, enter at least three proposed company names in Chinese and a romanized counterpart, choose ownership form limited liability, select business scope covering international media relations and crisis public relations agency under ISIC 7310 and NAICS 541820, and upload the scanned passports or business registration certificates of all shareholders. The examiner verifies national enterprise name database conflicts, prohibited or misleading word elements, and protection of well-known marks. If any name is unavailable, the examiner will approve an alternative ranking only after reviewing all three submissions. After approval, the system issues a digital Name Approval Notice valid for six months, during which the company must proceed with formal registration.
required_dossiers: Name Pre-approval Application Form
Passport or corporate registration certificate copies of all shareholders
Power of attorney for the authorized incorporation agent
Memorandum setting out the intended business scope in English and Chinese translation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected due to a name conflict or prohibited wording, file a fresh name pre-approval application or seek administrative reconsideration before SAMR within 15 days of refusal; the proposed name may be edited and resubmitted without an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Filing of Articles of Association and Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Enterprise Integration One-Stop Registration Portal; information is automatically shared with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) for foreign investment information reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the signed Joint Venture Contract and Articles of Association, ensure the Chinese text is controlling, and enter the integrated registration form on the SAMR one-stop portal. Tick the Foreign Investment Information Report tab and answer all questions identifying the beneficial owners, actual control, investment method, proposed business scope and material liabilities. Foreign shareholders must provide a certificate of incorporation or passport, translated and apostilled or notarized if requested. Upload the landlord's property title certificate, lease agreement, registered office confirmation, and scanned original identity documents of the legal representative, directors, supervisors, manager, and company secretary. The system automatically transmits the report to MOFCOM. Reviewing officers check the name approval, legal representative's eligibility, capital subscription schedule, and equity structure for consistency with the negative-list admission. If the application is accepted, a preliminary acceptance reference number is generated.
required_dossiers: Joint Venture Contract signed by all shareholders
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Foreign investor corporate registration certificate or passport copy, apostilled as applicable
Identity documents of legal representative, directors, supervisor, and general manager
Rent contract and property title certificate for the registered office
Foreign Investment Information Report completed online
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR or MOFCOM issues a query or suspension, correct the identified deficiencies within 15 working days through the one-stop portal; if the activity touches a restricted sector under the foreign investment negative list, modify the business scope or obtain the required sectoral approval before resubmitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal Market Entity Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal or District Market Supervision and Administration Bureau under SAMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the local SAMR enterprise registration platform and complete the formal Application for Formation Registration of a Foreign-Funded Limited Liability Company. Attach the certificate of name pre-approval, the final Articles of Association, the Foreign Investment Information Report record, proof of domicile, and the personal identity and appointment documents for the statutory officers. The examiner verifies that the subscribed capital schedule is consistent with the shareholders' contribution obligations, that the board composition respects supervisor independence, and that the contemplated public relations activities are not in a prohibited or restricted foreign investment sector. On approval, SAMR issues the Business License with a Unified Social Credit Code and date of establishment, at which point the Company lawfully exists. The applicant can print the electronic license immediately and may order a paper copy from the registry window. The formal registration application must be filed within six months of the name approval; otherwise the name reservation lapses.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Formation and Registration of a Limited Liability Company
Name Approval Certificate issued in Step 1
Articles of Association and Joint Venture Contract
Proof of registered office lease and landlord property title
Identity and appointment documents of directors, legal representative, supervisor and manager
Foreign Investment Information Report reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or suspended, correct the noted formal deficiencies and resubmit the same application; if the rejection is based on legal interpretation, apply for administrative reconsideration before the next-higher SAMR organ or bring an administrative litigation petition under the Administrative Litigation Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Seal Carving, Tax Registration, Social Insurance Registration, and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau authorized seal engraving office; State Taxation Administration China Electronic Tax Service; local social insurance and housing fund agencies; licensed commercial bank under People's Bank of China settlement account rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Business License, take the license and founding documents to an engraving house designated by the local Public Security Bureau to carve the company seal, finance seal, contract seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal, and file the seal record within the prescribed period. Complete tax registration with the State Taxation Administration on the China Electronic Tax Service, including corporation income tax, value added tax, withholding agent status, and invoice quota; the deadline is 30 calendar days after the Business License is issued. Open a basic deposit account at a licensed bank and, for foreign exchange purposes, complete the SAFE capital account procedure with the chosen bank for the foreign shareholder's capital injection. Register the Company with social insurance, housing fund, and medical care for any employees. Failure to complete these registrations may lead to late fees and administrative penalties; therefore each filing should be checked item by item.
required_dossiers: Original Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Seal engraving approval certificate issued by the Public Security Bureau
Legal representative identity document
Articles of Association and board resolution appointing bank signatories
Tax registration forms and invoice quota application
Bank account opening application and beneficial ownership statements
Office lease or property ownership certificate
Employee registration and social insurance forms, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For late tax or social insurance registration, submit a written explanation and pay any applicable late fees through the online portals; for delays or rejections in the SAFE capital account procedure, return to the designated commercial bank with corrected cross-border remittance documentation and, if necessary, appeal to the local SAFE branch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Instrument Adoption and Corporate Statutory Records Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors, corporate legal counsel, and SAMR change filing window if any registered item is amended
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting after the Business License is issued and have the Board formally adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, approving the share subscription record, the selected banks, the registered office, and the appointed legal representative, directors, and supervisor. Open the corporate statutory books: shareholder register, board minute book, share capital contribution ledger, and seal register. Adopt authorization policies for bank signatories, contract approvals, and corporate seal use. File any changes to the legal representative or registered office with SAMR if the board decision alters information already contained in the Business License. Minutes should be dated, signed, archived, and served on each director. A custodian must be assigned and all statutory records retained for at least ten years under current records-relevant regulations.
required_dossiers: Signed minutes and written consent of the First Board Meeting
Shareholder register and subscribed capital ledger
Board minute book and corporate seal register
Bank signatory authorization forms
Governance policies for contract execution, seal use, and treasury operations
Domicile and officer information if a SAMR change filing is triggered
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any statutory record is found defective, ratify an amending board resolution and replace or supplement the record without delay; if an incorrect filing has already been submitted to SAMR, use the online change registration module or submit an application for correction with the issuing registry before regulatory deadlines expire.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing board jurisdiction attaches to an ISIC 7310 overseas public relations and media communications firm because the enterprise operates as an office-based professional services company without physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facilities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory operating or manufacturing permit is required for pure public relations consulting, media relations, crisis communications, and digital advisory services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment EIA procedure not triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no construction, manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing project is being developed; no full EIA report, no simplified EIA registration, and no environmental acceptance inspection is required for the ordinary office lease.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the enterprise generates no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, hazardous waste stream, or industrial effluent requiring quantitative compliance thresholds; only ordinary municipal solid waste and office waste handling apply through the building management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit, industrial structural load inspection, or hazardous workplace clearance is required for an office-based PR and communications firm. The landlord's existing commercial fire safety acceptance and ordinary office lease compliance remain the only relevant fire-safety obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online portal is the Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) platform operated by STA and its provincial and municipal tax bureaus. Newly incorporated foreign-invested entities complete tax registration through the integrated market entity registration system administered with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must be incorporated with SAMR, which issues a Business License bearing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). Under the multi-license integration reform, the USCC is the legal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for the enterprise and no separate tax registration certificate is issued. Step 2: Within 30 days after the Business License is issued, the JV must complete supplemental tax registration information through the e-Tax portal, including legal representative details, accounting standards, banking account information, VAT taxpayer status, and filing frequency. Step 3: The JV must elect or be classified as either a General VAT Taxpayer or a Small-Scale VAT Taxpayer; if projected annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, General VAT Taxpayer registration is mandatory. Step 4: For a foreign non-resident enterprise that has not incorporated a Chinese entity, a Non-Resident Enterprise Taxpayer Identification Number must be obtained by application to the competent STA office, either directly or through a withholding agent, before the non-resident may enjoy treaty benefits or execute domestic VAT withholding obligations. Step 5: The taxpayer must configure fully digitalized electronic invoicing through the national Electronic Invoice Service Platform, link its bank account for tax payment and refund settlement, and register its export/service-trade foreign exchange receipts with the relevant payment bank and tax filing records for zero-rating or exemption claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is a Chinese resident enterprise and is taxed as a separate entity under the Enterprise Income Tax Law on its worldwide income. It is not eligible for pass-through treatment; distributions to foreign shareholders are subject to withholding tax where applicable under domestic law and the relevant double tax treaty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide a check-the-box entity classification election, pass-through election, or hybrid mismatch election for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture. For non-resident enterprises, an analysis of whether an establishment or place of business exists in China governs profit attribution and income tax exposure, but this is a factual statutory determination rather than an elective regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All incorporated business entities must complete tax registration regardless of turnover. Mandatory General VAT Taxpayer registration applies when aggregate annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000. A Small-Scale VAT Taxpayer with monthly taxable sales not exceeding RMB 100,000, or quarterly taxable sales not exceeding RMB 300,000, may apply for the applicable VAT exemption, but this does not eliminate the VAT registration obligation. For the subject public relations and communication agency services supplied domestically, the applicable VAT rate is 6% as modern services, while the 13% headline standard rate applies to general goods and the 9% rate applies to certain goods and transportation/construction services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices must be issued through the STA national Electronic Invoice Service Platform. Since the nationwide rollout of fully digitalized electronic invoices, each invoice is cleared in real time through the Golden Tax System Phase IV and is assigned a unique invoice number and a verified QR code anti-fraud digital stamp. Authorised taxpayers and enterprise ERP systems may use STA-specified APIs to transmit invoice data for real-time authentication. Traditional paper fiscal stamping is replaced by digital anti-fraud validation; STA systems perform automated cross-matching of invoice issuance, VAT filing, payment, and export refund declarations to detect anomalies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for exported goods evidenced by a valid customs export declaration, and for enumerated cross-border services supplied to an overseas entity and wholly consumed outside China under Ministry of Finance and STA Circular No. 36 of 2016 and implementing rules. Enumerated qualifying service categories include R&D services, design services, software services, information system services, business process management services, offshore outsourcing, and technical services. Public relations and communication agency services are generally classified as modern services at a domestic VAT rate of 6%; when supplied to an overseas client and fully consumed outside China, they may qualify for VAT exemption rather than automatic zero-rating/refund unless the arrangement falls within the enumerated offshore outsourcing or business process management service categories. To claim zero-rating or exemption, the taxpayer must demonstrate that the service is supplied to a non-resident enterprise, is not connected with Chinese real estate or goods or other Chinese services, is not consumed in China, is supported by a cross-border contract, and that the foreign currency consideration has been or will be repatriated into China through a recognised banking channel.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Form (export bill of entry) for physical goods; not applicable to pure service exports
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical movement of goods across customs boundaries where goods are exported
Commercial invoice and packing list issued under the relevant export contract
Bank foreign exchange receipt voucher or Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Chinese bank evidencing receipt, settlement, or verification of export/service-trade proceeds
Cross-border service contract and engagement letter describing the overseas client, scope of work, and offshore consumption
Certificate of foreign client status and supporting evidence that the service was performed and consumed entirely outside China
Statutory VAT invoice, preferably a fully digitalized electronic invoice, correctly coded and issued for the export transaction
Export tax rebate or zero-rating application and service trade foreign exchange receipt filing submitted through the STA electronic tax system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may conduct post-export audits and require production of customs declarations, bank SWIFT receipts, foreign exchange settlement vouchers, service performance records, contracts, and offshore consumption evidence. If a zero-rating or exemption claim is rejected or found to be unsupported, the taxpayer must repay the refunded or exempted VAT, pay late payment surcharges of 0.05% per day on the unpaid amount, and may incur administrative fines ranging from 50% to five times the amount of tax involved under Article 63 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Levying. Fraudulent export tax refund or zero-rating claims may be prosecuted as criminal offences under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, with penalties including monetary fines, confiscation of property, and imprisonment up to life imprisonment for especially serious cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese yuan (CNY) operates under a managed floating exchange rate regime with strict capital account controls, while current account transactions are generally convertible subject to documentary review. Foreign-invested enterprises (FIEs) such as the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must obtain Foreign Exchange Registration (FDI) from SAFE before opening a capital account. Capital inflows for registered equity investment may be freely converted into CNY under the capital account convertibility liberalisation, but outbound remittances of profits, dividends, or liquidated funds require verification of audited financials, tax clearance certificates, and compliance with the real-business-transaction principle. Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory surrender since the 2012 reform, yet all foreign currency receipts must be repatriated to China within 180 days of customs declaration and reported through the Trade Monitoring System. Profit remittances face additional hurdles: the joint venture must submit an audit report, tax payment proof, and board resolution, and each remittance must be individually authorised by the designated bank. Prudent treasury planning must account for repatriation lead times, the risk of transfer pricing adjustments, and the possibility that SAFE may require supporting documentation for cross-border payments exceeding USD 500,000. In practice, current account convertibility is efficient for genuine trade and service payments, but capital account outflows are slow and highly scrutinised, making early engagement with bank compliance and SAFE essential.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current SAFE rules (as amended), export proceeds collected in foreign currency are not required to be mandatorily surrendered to the central bank. Exporters may retain these funds in a foreign currency settlement account or voluntarily convert them into CNY. However, all export proceeds from goods exported from mainland China must be repatriated to China within 180 days after the date of export customs declaration. The exporter must register the receipt in the Trade Monitoring System and ensure the payment is consistent with the declared transaction. There is no statutory minimum conversion ratio; enterprises may choose to hold the entirety of their export earnings in foreign currency, subject to the bank's risk classification and SAFE post-verification. Failure to repatriate within the 180-day window can trigger regulatory sanctions, a downgrade of the entity's classification, and mandatory on-site inspections.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI) and Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI) and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account (FDI) and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore financial technology EMIs (electronic money institutions) are not viable for servicing a China-based entity. The PBOC and SAFE maintain a closed licensing regime for payment institutions and foreign-currency clearing services. Non-bank financial institutions that do not hold a domestic Payment Business License are prohibited from opening deposit accounts, executing FX conversions, or conducting cross-border settlement on behalf of Chinese legal persons. In practice, foreign digital banks and EMIs such as Revolut Business or Wise cannot provide compatible RMB clearing or direct debit/credit rails within mainland China. Any attempt to route treasury flows through an unlicensed EMI would trigger immediate red flags in bank KYC reviews, potentially leading to account closure and regulatory penalties. The only lawful approach is to use a licensed domestic bank for all CNY and FX operations; offshore EMI accounts may be used only for ancillary receivables from overseas clients, provided they strictly comply with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange's requirement that all cross-border trade payments be settled through designated domestic banks. Therefore, the strategic treasury blueprint should rely exclusively on Tier-1 Chinese commercial banks for operational liquidity management.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the legal entity account opening, the statutory director or an authorised agent (with a notarised and legalised power of attorney) must appear physically at the bank branch in mainland China for an in-person interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for foreign-invested enterprises. The joint venture's legal representative (typically the chairman or general manager) must be present if he/she is a foreign national; alternatively, the Chinese co-investor's empowered director can attend with a board resolution and a notarised power of attorney originating from the overseas parent. Banks may accept a video-call interview in exceptional COVID-19-related circumstances, but only after the foreign director has completed a face-to-face authentication at a Chinese embassy or consulate and the original documents have been countersigned by the bank's compliance officer. In all cases, the bank's KYC team will conduct a verification call to the registered office and may request a site visit if the business profile appears high risk. The substitution of a local proxy without explicit notarised authority from the board of directors is a common reason for rejection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) ownership chain is unclear or complex, particularly when the overseas parent is held through multiple private trust or nominee structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete UBO disclosure form provided by the joint venture, supported by a notarised shareholding certificate for each holding layer up to the ultimate individual beneficial owner, plus an organisational chart with percentage ownership, copies of passports for all natural person UBOs, and a signed declaration confirming no undisclosed third-party interests. Additionally, the bank may require a certified legal opinion from a PRC law firm confirming the validity of the chain and absence of shell company characteristics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected sanction exposure or PEP (Politically Exposed Person) status of a director or UBO, especially where the entity has counterparties in jurisdictions subject to Chinese or UN sanctions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A sanctions screening report generated from an independent commercial database (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv) for all directors, UBOs, and senior managers, dated within the last 90 days; a signed anti-money laundering self-certification; professional references from two existing banks; and, where applicable, a PEP declaration with a list of public offices and a risk-mitigation statement. If the name triggers a partial match, a detailed name-searching protocol and a document proving the difference in identity or date of birth must be provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The foreign investor's source of funds for capital injection appears incompatible with its stated business size or financial statements, potentially indicating money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified bank statements of the foreign investor for the past 12 months, audited financial statements for the last 3 years, a sworn source-of-funds letter explaining the business rationale for the investment, the signed joint venture contract, and, if the capital originates from corporate profits, copies of the prior year's tax returns and dividend distribution approval to demonstrate economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity inconsistency — the entity declares a PR agency (ISIC 7310) but payment patterns or transaction partners suggest involvement in trade or consultancy not aligned with the primary licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed business plan describing the services delivered to overseas clients, executed client contracts and master service agreements, sample invoices and media purchase orders, proof of professional qualifications of key staff, and a comprehensive AML risk assessment for the payment rails (retainer ACH and wire) showing that each transaction will be backed by a contract and a service completion report. The bank may also request a site inspection or the appointment of a qualified local compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection from the foreign investor must be executed through a registered FDI capital account opened at a designated domestic bank. The investor should instruct the overseas remitting bank to use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 622 (foreign direct investment) or the approved SAFE code for equity injection, and the remittance currency should be in USD, EUR, HKD, or CNY (if permitted under the free-trade zone). The joint venture must complete the Foreign Exchange Registration (FDI) with SAFE via the bank, and the bank will issue a payment confirmation and handle capital verification through an accounting firm. The funds can only be credited to the Capital Escrow Account, after which they can be converted to CNY based on real transaction needs (payment orders) — the so-called 'payment-negative list' approach. For capital contributions exceeding USD 5 million, the bank's head-office compliance review is mandatory. All capital inflows must be accompanied by the original joint venture contract, the business licence, and the approval certificate (if still applicable). Once converted, the CNY funds are transferred to the Basic Operational Currency Account and cannot be reversed to foreign exchange without SAFE approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border outbound payments for trade and service settlements (e.g., retainer fees to overseas media partners, payments for advertising technology platforms) can be cleared via SWIFT MT103 for regular wire transfers, documentary collections (D/P or D/A), or commercial letters of credit (L/C) when robust security is needed. For service imports, the bank requires presentation of the underlying service contract, invoice, a proof of service delivery (e.g., signed timesheets or media purchase confirmations), and a certificate of tax payment (withholding tax and VAT). For goods-related disbursements (e.g., promotional materials), a customs declaration and bill of lading must be submitted. All payments must be consistent with the scope of business and the registered trade code. Payments exceeding USD 300,000 may trigger additional authenticity verification and reporting to SAFE. The use of renminbi cross-border settlement (CIPS) is also permissible for transactions with counterparties in countries that have signed a local-currency settlement agreement with China, reducing FX conversion costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instrids: Forward contracts (FX Forwards) with a maturity not exceeding 12 months, executed through the domestic bank under a real-currency exposure from trade or investment balances, requiring supporting commercial documents for hedging purpose.

FX Swaps (Swap of principal and interest) allowed for converting CNY to foreign currency and back where the underlying transaction is genuine trade facilitation, with SAFE registration of the hedging exposure.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) are permissible for long-term capital projects, but only with the approval of the domestic bank and SAFE where the FX positions arise from actual debt or equity investments.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are NOT permitted onshore for mainland Chinese entities due to capital account restrictions; offshore NDF markets may be accessed only by non-resident counterparties, and no mainland entity may hedge through offshore NDFs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report (annual return to the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System under the Interim Regulations on Enterprise Information Publicity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local market regulation bureaus
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year from January 1 to June 30, covering the immediately preceding financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If not submitted by June 30, the company is entered on the Business Abnormal List after a 10-working-day grace period; after three consecutive years of non-rectification, it is transferred to the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List, exposing the legal representative to directorship restrictions, joint credit punishment and eventual compulsory deregistration or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report under the PRC Foreign Investment Law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM), administered with SAMR via the integrated foreign investment reporting platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by June 30 for the preceding calendar year, filed together with the annual enterprise credit information report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing triggers a rectification order; non-correction within the stated period attracts an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000. Persistent failure can lead to revocation of the joint venture business licence and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Final Settlement (annual CIT filing and self-assessment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration and the local competent tax offices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the year following each tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a daily overdue surcharge of 0.05 percent of the unpaid tax; underreporting penalties range from 50 percent to 100 percent of the tax undercharged. Tax authorities may freeze bank accounts, seize assets, publish blacklists, and initiate enforced collection, ultimately leading to deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Audit Report of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and shareholders; submitted to SAMR, MOFCOM and tax authorities as required in support of annual filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed in time for the May 31 CIT final settlement and the June 30 annual report filing window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A foreign-invested enterprise that fails to obtain a clean statutory audit report from a PRC-licensed CPA firm is non-compliant with the Accounting Law and Foreign Investment Law; regulators may reject the annual filing, impose administrative fines, disallow deductions and risk compulsory strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered address, licence particulars and enterprise information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR local registration office and State Administration of Foreign Exchange where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in directors, shareholders, registered capital, address or scope must be filed within 30 calendar days of the event; no separate anniversary licence renewal is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely change registration exposes the company and responsible legal representative to warnings or fines, adverse credit records and suspension of administrative services; material concealment can trigger administrative deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: China imposes blanket statutory audit requirements on every foreign-invested enterprise, including a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, with no de minimis balance-sheet, turnover or headcount exemption; the quantitative trigger is therefore any positive paid-in capital, any revenue, or any employee count. In addition, if a domestic small enterprise elects PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards, independent audit remains compulsory where required by state-owned, listed, financial-sector or public-interest status, or where a competent authority mandates the audit for supervisory reasons.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC GAAP / ASBE), which are substantially converged with IFRS; the JV must maintain statutory books under PRC GAAP and may prepare an IFRS-aligned consolidation package for the foreign parent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The JV confirms beneficial ownership annually through the ownership section of the SAMR Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report each January to June. Any transfer or pledge of registered capital, change in shareholders, or change in the ultimate beneficial owner must additionally be updated in the statutory registers and filed with SAMR, MOFCOM and the tax bureau within 30 calendar days of the change. On-site UBO and share-holding registers must be kept available for inspection by SAMR, PBOC and anti-money laundering supervisors.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 to USD 4,000 per annum for a registered office and local corporate secretarial agent in major PRC business cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to USD 8,000 per annum for a certified CPA statutory audit of a low-risk, non-listed JV with an overseas PR communications scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard Corporate Income Tax rate for resident enterprises and for non-resident enterprises with a China-establishment/PE on China-source income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Low-Profit Enterprises enjoy a preferential 20% rate with an effective tax burden of 5% on qualifying taxable income (subject to policy sunset extension); High-New Technology Enterprises pay 15%; encouraged software/IC production enterprises may access a two-year exemption followed by a 50% reduced rate; eligible R&D expenses receive an additional 100% super-deduction; certain free-zone/encouraged-industry regimes (e.g., Western Region, Hainan Free Trade Port, Lingang) provide 15% rate benefits; no national participation exemption is available for foreign dividends, but a unilateral Foreign Tax Credit is available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form A100000 - 中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表（A类）) filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration 电子税务局 / e-tax filing system, together with supporting schedules including A101010, A102010, A105000, A106000, A107010, A107012, A109000, and withholding schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement plus quarterly provisional prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed and settled within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (usually by May 31 of the following calendar year); quarterly provisional CIT prepayments must be filed within 15 days after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from advertising, public relations, media relations, crisis communications, retainer services, and consulting fees recognized under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report revenue on an accrual basis, net of VAT. For a Sino-Foreign Equity JV that is an overseas PR communications firm, include all China-source revenue and any global service revenue performed from or connected to the China establishment. Ensure that intercompany service fees from foreign affiliates are priced at arm's length; if the JV acts as a commissionaire or pays a foreign affiliate for subcontracted work, reclassify or adjust revenue to avoid artificial shifting. Warn: invoicing through a Hong Kong or offshore intermediary for services physically performed in China may create a deemed PE of the JV and trigger additional tax leakage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs directly associated with service delivery, including salaries of PR consultants, media purchase costs, production costs, and subcontractor fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match costs against Box 1 revenue in accordance with accrual accounting. Expenses paid to overseas group companies must satisfy the 'actual cost' requirement and arm's length standard; if any foreign vendor is a related party, verify whether the expense is a managed cost sharing or a recharged cost and support with contemporaneous documentation. Any unsupported allocation from a Hong Kong/Overseas parent to a Chinese JV should be reversed for tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (A100000-3) - Taxes and Surcharges (Tax and Other Charges)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Levies other than income tax, including city maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp duty, and land-related taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only taxes and surcharges actually borne by the entity are deductible. Withholding taxes on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties are not deductible CIT liabilities. If the JV is designated as the withholding agent for non-resident service providers, any WHT borne by the JV under a gross-up arrangement is generally non-deductible unless specifically permitted; adjust in Box 8 accordingly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Period expenses: selling expenses (media placements, commissions), administrative expenses (management salaries, office rent, professional fees), and financial expenses (interest, FX losses, bank charges).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow management fees paid to foreign shareholders that merely constitute profit distribution rather than remuneration for actual services. International PR agency network fees must be supported by evidence of services actually rendered, costing, and benefit received by the JV. Interest on intercompany loans must not exceed the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin-capitalisation ratio (5:1 for qualifying financial institutions); otherwise excessive interest is non-deductible. Personal expenses of expatriate shareholders/directors are strictly non-deductible unless clearly connected to business and substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (A100000-7) - Impairment Losses and Fair Value Movements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Asset impairment provisions, fair value changes on financial assets, and gains or losses on disposal of assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Generally, impairment losses on receivables, inventory, fixed assets, and goodwill are not deductible until actually realized, unless in compliance with the special tax rules. For an overseas PR agency, significant accounts receivable from foreign group companies may be subject to transfer pricing scrutiny; a non-arm's length write-off receivable from the foreign parent must be reversed and taxed. Do not deduct the notional cost of intercompany provided services for which no payable has been recognised.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (A100000-8/9/10) - Non-Operating Income and Non-Operating Expense
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating items such as asset write-off gains, penalty income, donations, losses, and compensation payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include deemed dividends from low-tax-region subsidiaries. For PRC JV, if any foreign shareholder provides below-market loans and forgives debt, the forgiveness may be taxable as deemed income under GAAR. Non-charitable donations are not deductible unless made through qualified Chinese charities within the statutory 12% cap. Fines and tax penalties are never deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax computed as operating profit plus non-operating income minus non-operating expense.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the accounting profit is the base before Chinese CIT adjustments. For the non-resident shareholder, this amount does not yet reflect withholding tax; profits after CIT will be subject to dividend withholding when distributed. If the JV reinvests profits or makes a zero distribution, no dividend WHT arises until actual or deemed distribution. Carry out a book-to-tax reconciliation to detect PE-related misclassification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between accounting profit and taxable income: indicates additions and deductions such as non-tax revenue, an actual tax integrated with tax law, advertising and business entertainment caps, impairment provisions, fines, excess interest, TP adjustments, and losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory adjustments for related-party payments that are excessive due to non-arm's length pricing, pure shell mark-ups, royalty payments to connected parties without economic substance, and unreported Chinese withholding on cross-border income. Also adjust holiday/year-end accruals that are not paid within the statutory filing period. For the overseas PR firm, payments to a UK/HK group marketing office must be tested against the OECD 'benefit test' and 'arm's-length value test'; any international marketing fee that is not actually incurred or not benefiting the JV must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit adjusted by add-backs and deductions; the base for computing CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If taxable income includes China-source income derived through a PE plus global income attributable to the PE, report the full amount. If the entity is a pure non-resident without PE, the tax on passive China-source income is not reported on this form but is withheld under Form F501/withholding schedule. For a resident JV, all worldwide income is taxable; any double taxation relief must be claimed through the Foreign Tax Credit schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate applied to taxable income; generally 25%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select preferential rate code if the JV qualifies for 15% high-tech rate or 20% small low-profit rate, or if the JV is located in a preferential zone and holds a qualification certificate. For non-resident withholding income, the corresponding rate is not this Box; instead use the 10% default WHT or a DTA-reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable tax rate, adjusted by exemption/reduction amount for small low-profit enterprises and other preferential rate regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the JV, compute CIT on the taxable income after applying all preferential rate reductions. Ensure that if a foreign tax credit is claimed, the credit cannot exceed the PRC tax on the relevant foreign-source income using the territorial apportionment method. If the JV underpaid due to transfer pricing adjustments, the difference will be payable together with penal interest from the due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 (A100000-15) - Credits, Prepayments and Balance Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, loss carryover, quarterly prepayments withheld by customers, and the remaining balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The final settlement must be completed by May 31. Any overpaid WHT on outbound dividends may be refundable if the payee later proves treaty eligibility, but such refund arrangements must be agreed with the in-charge tax bureau. If the entity has made payments to non-resident employees or shareholders on behalf of them, it must simultaneously file the non-resident withholding schedules and remit withholding tax within 7 days of the payment date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fines from RMB 200 up to RMB 10,000 plus 0.05% per day overdue interest on unpaid tax; false or nontrivial underreporting triggers an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% (5x) of the underpaid tax under Article 63 of the Law on Administration of Tax Collection. Late payment surcharge continues until payment is made. Failure to file the annual return can result in automatic assessment under Article 40 of the Tax Collection Law. Tax evasion exceeding RMB 50,000 share of unpaid tax constitutes a criminal offence and can result in imprisonment of up to seven years plus fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory rate for dividends distributed by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder, unless reduced by a tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The JV (or the non-resident shareholder seeking a refund) must follow the STA Bulletin 2019 No.35 procedure: (1) Obtain and present a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority in the contracting state; (2) Complete the tax treaty benefit application form and a Beneficial Ownership declaration, supported by board resolutions, shareholding registers, annual reports, and evidence of substantive economic activity in the residence jurisdiction; (3) Provide detailed breakdown of the dividend, including date of profit-resolution, gross amount, foreign shareholding ratio, and whether the shareholder holds at least a 25% equity interest (for 5% treaty rate under many DTAs, including Hong Kong/Macau); (4) File the withholding return and schedule with the local tax authority at the time of distribution, usually within 7 days of the resolution, and pay the WHT; failure to obtain a valid TRC before filing will result in the default 10% rate and a potential penalty for late payment. The withholding agent, not the non-resident shareholder, bears the statutory obligation to withhold and remit tax; if not withheld, the JV is directly assessed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on outbound interest and royalties is 10% (for non-resident enterprises without a PE or effective PE connection). Under many Chinese DTA, interest treaty rates can be 10%, 7% (e.g., China-Hong Kong), or 0% for certain government financial institutions; royalties are commonly reduced to 5%-10%, with China-Hong Kong and some other treaties allowing 5% for industrial, commercial, and scientific equipment royalties. Royalty deductions in the JV must satisfy the 'authenticity, necessity, reasonableness' standard and cannot simply be used to strip profits out of China.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CNY: Contemporaneous Local File/Master File is mandatory where annual related-party transactions exceed: (i) CNY 200 million for tangible asset transfers; (ii) CNY 100 million for intangible asset transfers; (iii) CNY 100 million for financial asset transfers; (iv) CNY 40 million for other related-party transactions (including service fees; royalty payments; interest). If the JV has any related-party transaction with a low-tax jurisdiction (effective rate below 12.5%), the threshold is suspended and documentation is required for smaller amounts.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China does not have a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but the GAAR under Article 47 of the PRC Corporate Income Tax Law and the 'substance over form' doctrine apply. For treaty benefits, the contracting-state resident must perform Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in that state; a Hong Kong or other intermediary with only a mailbox, nominee director, or paper board will be considered a conduit and denied treaty benefits. The Chinese CIT administration uses BEPS Action 3, Action 6, and Action 8 principles to re-characterize transactions without economic substance. The JV must maintain substance evidence for any transaction with its non-resident parent and must not simply re-invoice global PR costs through an offshore entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Tax Collection Law / Criminal Law)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV deliberately conceals China-source PR and media agency revenue by booking it to a Hong Kong sibling, fabricates advisory invoices from an overseas shell company, overstates deductible service fees to the foreign parent, or manipulates contracts to shift profit with no economic substance. This includes failing to file the annual CIT return or filing a false return with materially understated taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the PRC Law on Administration of Tax Collection: administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% from the due date until payment, and correction order. If the amount of tax evaded exceeds certain thresholds and is declared a criminal offence under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law, the entity is fined and the responsible directors are subject to criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly signs a false tax return or supervises a false invoicing scheme will be personally liable to the extent of unpaid taxes recovered through piercing the corporate veil under Article 20 of the PRC Companies Law. The personal assets of the director may be seized in restitution; the director will be placed of a tax blacklist, get a travel ban and exit-control (出境限制) by the immigration authorities, and can face imprisonment for up to 7 years together with a criminal fine and forfeiture of illegal gains.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV pays dividends, interest, or management fees to a Hong Kong or other foreign company that is the ultimate parent but has no business substance, no employees, no office, and no COO/CIGA in the claimed treaty jurisdiction; the arrangement is used solely to reduce China withholding tax from 10% to 5% or to obtain an exemption from tax on royalties/interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 47 of the PRC Corporate Income Tax Law and Implementing Regulations Article 120 empower the tax authority to disregard the offshore entity in an arrangement lacking reasonable commercial purpose. The taxes will be re-assessed at the statutory 10% rate, plus interest and an administrative penalty under Article 63/64 of the Tax Collection Law. The tax authority can also invoke the OECD BEPS PPT/LOB rule under the DTA, denying treaty benefits and re-characterizing the payment as a taxable dividend.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the circular of State Administration of Taxation on 'Strong exposure and control of high-end tax-reducing arrangements', legal representatives and financial officers who design or execute a treaty-abusive structure can be held personally liable for penalties and interest. The corporate veil may be pierced, and the director's personal assets will be used to satisfy the adjusted tax. Travel restrictions and tax-information 'blacklisting' (重大税收违法失信案件) apply. If the arrangement includes forgery of TRC or financial statements, criminal punishment for tax fraud can be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Related-Party Disclosures (TP non-compliance)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV fails to prepare or submit Local File/Master File and related-party transaction declarations despite having related-party service fees, royalties, management charges, or intercompany loans that exceed the regulatory thresholds. The JV also fails to make contemporaneous market-based comparability analysis for cross-border services, uses a fictitious CUP, or consistently reports operating losses while paying high margins to the overseas group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 62 of the Tax Collection Law imposes a fixed penalty of RMB 10,000 for failure to file related-party declarations; transfer pricing adjustment may be made prospectively and retrospectively, with a special tax adjustment to impute taxable income. If the under-reporting is due to malice or false documentation, the penalty can rise to 50% of the adjusted additional tax, plus 5-year accrual interest at the benchmark rate. The PRC tax authority may also impose a secondary adjustment if the corresponding profits are not repatriated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and CFOs who sign incomplete TP documents or sign off on a deliberately ineffective transfer-pricing policy can have the corporate veil pierced under the Company Law. The tax authority may request an administrative investigation of the director's personal bank accounts and assets if intercompany payments disguised as 'expenses' actually benefited the director personally. The responsible individuals are included on the serious tax violation 'blacklist', leading to travel bans, a ban on high-consumption activities, and disqualification from being legal representatives. In cases of fraud, criminal liability under Article 201 applies.
